subject: botany
question_text: The following events occur during the various phases of the cell cycle. Name the phase against each: (a) disintegration of the nuclear membrane (b) appearance of the nucleolus (c) division of the centromere (d) replication of DNA.

steps.label: (a) and (b)

lines.text: Prophase. It breaks down at the end of
The nucleolus and the nuclear membrane both

steps.why: Prophase and telophase are opposites: what disappears in prophase, the nuclear membrane and the nucleolus, comes back in telophase. Pairing them that way makes both answers one decision.
common_mistakes: Answering metaphase for the nuclear membrane. By metaphase it has already gone.
Answering prophase for the nucleolus. In prophase the nucleolus disappears.
steps.memory_tip: Prophase takes the nucleus apart, telophase puts it back together.
steps.margin_note: One line each. No explanation is needed.

steps.label: (c) and (d)
steps.why: The centromere splits only when the sister chromatids are pulled apart, which is the defining event of anaphase; DNA replication is the defining event of S phase. Each answer is the phase named after its own event.
common_mistakes: Answering metaphase for centromere division. In metaphase the centromeres are lined up, still whole.
Answering G₁ or G₂ for DNA replication. Both gap phases make proteins, not DNA.
steps.memory_tip: Name the phase by its own event: S for synthesis, anaphase for apart.
steps.margin_note: Four one-word answers in all. Write the phase names only.

insider_note: Four one-word answers. Write the phase name only — a wrong extra sentence can lose a mark the name had already earned.
